text:
Mikael Backlund is 37, has played 1,170 games as a Flame, and having the kind of start that gets a veteran's age blamed for everything. Three goals and eight points in 22 games looks like decline. Our numbers say it mostly isn't. He has three goals on 5.7 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and Calgary has scored about eight fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice.

His game is still there in the tracking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones data has him in the 97th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists and the 83rd for chances from in front of the net, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 88th percentile at taking chances away last season. Calgary's five-on-five share is a little better with him than without. He won the King Clancy in 2022-23. On a team at 9% to make the playoffs in our numbers, he deserves better luck than he is getting.
